The DRM Definition of a Document
A file containing Unstructured and/or Semi-Structured Data    Resources. A discrete and unique electronic aggregation of data produced with the intent of conveying information.

All data within a document may be in the same format (e.g., text), or a document may be a composite that consists of sets of data in a variety of formats (e.g., MS Word files containing embedded graphics). 

The term “discrete” implies that a document requires no linkage to other data to convey its meaning. 

The term “unique” implies that each instance or version of a document can be distinguished from all others (i.e., it can be assigned a unique identifying number).

The DRM Definition of a Document
Documents may be unstructured
The document follows no rigid, machine interpretable structural convention or it may contain self describing metadata that is machine interpretable. 
For example: An ASCII text document

Documents may be semi-structured
The documents conforms to a machine interpretable structural convention or contains embedded self-describing metadata that is machine interpretable. 
A Microsoft Word document with headings and sub-headings is considered semi-structured, as is a XHTML document.

Relevant DRMDocument Related Data Services
Publication 
(Structured data or documents to aggregate documents): Publication is the process of assembling a document from its component pieces, putting into a desired format and disseminating it to target databases. The payload of this type of service is a document. 

Document Translation (Document to document)
 Document translation is the process of transforming a document from its original format to a format required to support a target application. The transformations may be structural (e.g., transforming MS Word to PDF format), language-oriented (e.g., changing English to French), or special purpose (e.g., the development of abstracts from longer documents.) The payload of this type of service is a document.

DRM Guidance on Quality, Security, Privacy, and Confidentiality
Within A Community of Interest (COI):
Establish Data Stewardship

Define the Policies.  Use the following “policy buckets”:

Data is available for open, unrestricted access 
Data is accessible only to a group 
Data access is a function of the person (his or her identity), data about that person (e.g., current position), and data about the environment (e.g., physical location) 
Data is self protecting through digital rights management or similar technologies  
Implement the policies within the Data Sharing Services

So…What’s the Way Ahead for Copyrighting and Marking US Government Works?
A FEA Profile that builds on the DRM Constructs:
Notional Components:
Stewards in a COI identify material that needs copyright protection.
Focus on Publication and Translation Services
Tag the documents at publication (e.g. source referencing)
If non-repudiation is needed, sign the documents
(Also what to think about records and records management here.)
If the documents are very sensitive, wrap them in a Digital Rights Management capable package.

Need to agree on voluntary consensus standards for document tagging for copyright.
The Data Architecture Subcommittee can help.

Summary
FEA DRM provides an overarching construct.
While copyright and intellectual property is not specifically addressed, the model can be extended.
Federal level guidance could be addressed in a profile.
The Federal Data Architecture Subcommittee (DAS) is ready to help.
